report.answer: A basketball is released from rest and falls straight down in slow motion. A projectile fit to its free-fall gives g = 1.63 ± 0.06 m/s², matching Moon gravity 1.62 and ruling out Earth 9.81. No air drag is needed and the overlay tracks the fall exactly to the ground.
assumptions: Camera still, motion vertical in plane facing camera
Scale from basketball itself: 0.24 ± 0.005 m diameter at same depth as fall

forks.label: Same drop on Earth
forks.why: Fall takes ~2.5x less time, shows 6x gravity difference.

forks.label: Ideal lunar vacuum
forks.why: Removes the tiny drag term to show vacuum free-fall is identical.

forks.label: Lunar bounce
forks.why: Continue past impact to measure bounciness on the Moon.

report.headline: Lunar gravity fall: g = 1.63 m/s²
